subject.title: fix: protect SMS webhook callback quota [AI]

question: Should SMS preserve a valid signed callback after the unauthenticated same-key budget is exhausted, or intentionally fail closed for every request on that key?
rationale: Before signature verification the handler cannot distinguish invalid traffic from a legitimate synchronous Twilio callback, while Twilio's default 4xx policy does not recover the rejected delivery.

options.title: Preserve authenticated delivery
options.body: Use bounded request guards and rejected-outcome accounting that cannot consume authenticated callback capacity, with same-key regression and HTTP proof.

options.title: Accept fail-closed denial
options.body: Keep the early gate only with explicit owner approval and documentation that same-key invalid traffic can suppress callbacks for one minute.

recommendation.title: Preserve authenticated delivery
recommendation.body: Use bounded request guards and rejected-outcome accounting that cannot consume authenticated callback capacity, with same-key regression and HTTP proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the SMS channel and authored and merged the latest security-relevant hardening in this handler.
